pss_menu_desc: Custom shaders on the game world, drawn underneath the HUD.
pss_enabled_desc: Master switch for everything in Screen Shaders.
pss_menu_controls_desc: Keys for the shaders, the split view and a draw capture.
pss_key_toggle_desc: Switches the shaders on and off, in the menu or in a heist.
pss_key_split_desc: Switches the side-by-side comparison on and off.
pss_key_capture_desc: Records two frames of the game's drawing to the BLT logs folder, for troubleshooting with the Tools page.
pss_menu_detail_desc: Smoother edges, restored texture detail and clean gradients.
pss_antialiasing_desc: Smooths jagged edges. FXAA: cheapest, softest. SMAA: sharp. SMAA T2x: smoother than SMAA, no trails. TAA: smoothest, but moving things can trail.
pss_aa_subpix_desc: FXAA only. How much thin detail is smoothed. Higher is softer.
pss_aa_edge_desc: FXAA only. How much contrast counts as an edge. Lower catches more edges and costs a little more.
pss_sharpen_desc: Restores texture detail without the halos of a plain sharpen. 0 turns it off. Bypassed while FSR upscale is on.
pss_upscale_desc: Redraws the frame with FSR 1.0 at the factor below. Above 1x: smoother edges. Below 1x: less shimmer, a little softer. Costs GPU time.
pss_upscale_scale_desc: Above 1x: smoother, costs more GPU time and video memory. Below 1x: cleaner and softer. 1x does neither.
pss_upscale_sharpness_desc: RCAS sharpening, applied after the frame is fitted back to your screen, above 1x. It takes the place of Sharpening (CAS) there; at 1x and below, Sharpening (CAS) applies. 0 turns it off.
pss_deband_desc: Smooths stepped bands in dark fog, skies and smoke while edges stay crisp. 0 turns it off.
pss_dither_desc: Fine, invisible noise that stops grading from bringing banding back. 0 turns it off.
pss_exposure_desc: Brightens or darkens the whole image before anything else. Eye adaptation adds on top.
pss_adapt_desc: Brightens dark places and settles bright ones, the way your eyes adjust. 0 turns it off.
pss_adapt_speed_desc: How fast your eyes adjust. Low values feel like walking from a street into a vault.
pss_adapt_key_desc: The brightness the image settles towards. Raise it for a brighter picture overall.
pss_adapt_min_desc: The most eye adaptation will darken a bright scene.
pss_adapt_max_desc: The most eye adaptation will brighten a dark scene.
pss_bloom_desc: Glow around bright lights and windows. 0 turns it off.
pss_bloom_threshold_desc: How bright something has to be before it glows.
pss_menu_colour_desc: White balance, tone and colour grading.
pss_temperature_desc: Warmer above 0, cooler below. Brightness is kept.
pss_tint_desc: Magenta above 0, green below. Brightness is kept.
pss_shadows_desc: Brings detail up out of dark areas while black stays black.
pss_highlights_desc: Pulls bright areas down so they keep detail. Below 0 brightens them.
pss_lift_desc: Raises or lowers the black floor. Small changes go a long way.
pss_gain_desc: Overall brightness from the top down.
pss_contrast_desc: A gentle S-curve. Below 0 flattens the image.
pss_saturation_desc: Colour strength across the whole image.
pss_vibrance_desc: Boosts muted colours more than strong ones, so skin and signs do not go neon.
pss_lut_desc: A look from the luts folder. Add any .cube file there and press Reload shaders on the Tools page.
pss_lut_mix_desc: How much of the colour grade is applied.
pss_menu_depth_desc: Clarity, obscurance, colour bloom and monocular cues. All work from the image alone, without depth.
pss_clarity_desc: Local contrast in the midtones, so surfaces and faces gain definition. Below 0 softens.
pss_obscurance_on_desc: Bloom in reverse: creases, corners and contact areas darken slightly. Never next to deep shadow.
pss_obscurance_desc: How much darker recesses get. The darkening is capped so shadows stay readable.
pss_obscurance_radius_desc: How far around each point it looks for darker surroundings.
pss_color_bloom_on_desc: Strong colours spread softly into their surroundings, like light bouncing off a painted wall. White light is left to Bloom.
pss_color_bloom_desc: How much colour spreads. The overall brightness stays the same.
pss_cues_on_desc: Helps shapes stand out from their background, using only what is already on screen. It cannot reveal anything hidden.
pss_cues_desc: Overall strength of the three cues below.
pss_cues_separation_desc: Local contrast where objects meet their background, kept soft so there are no halos.
pss_cues_depth_desc: Flat, low-contrast areas recede slightly, the way distance fades detail.
pss_cues_focus_desc: The edges of the screen soften slightly so the centre, where you look, keeps full detail.
pss_menu_lens_desc: Vignette, chromatic aberration, film grain, lens dirt and halation.
pss_vignette_desc: Darkens the corners to draw the eye in. 0 turns it off.
pss_chromatic_desc: A fringe of colour towards the edges of the screen. 0 turns it off.
pss_grain_desc: Fine moving grain, strongest in the midtones. 0 turns it off.
pss_mood_hurt_desc: Badly hurt, the edges close in and the colour drains; on the floor, further still. It lifts as you heal, and your saved grade is never changed.
pss_mood_assault_desc: Stealth reads a shade cooler and quieter; once it is loud, warmer and harder. Reads the assault state everyone can already see.
pss_dirt_on_desc: Dust on the lens, lit by the bright light in the frame and thrown to the opposite side. With no bright light in view it disappears instead of greying the picture.
pss_dirt_desc: How brightly the dust catches the light. 0 turns it off.
pss_dirt_offset_desc: How far the dust sits from the light across the glass. Higher throws it further to the opposite side.
pss_halation_on_desc: The warm bleed film gets around its brightest highlights. Only near-white areas feed it, so it stays separate from bloom.
pss_halation_desc: How much warm light bleeds around bright highlights. 0 turns it off.
pss_halation_threshold_desc: How bright something must be before it bleeds. Higher keeps it to lamps and windows.
pss_halation_tint_desc: How red the bleed goes. 0 leaves it the colour of the highlight itself.
pss_halation_radius_desc: How far the bleed spreads around a highlight.
pss_split_desc: The left half shows the untouched game and the right half the shaders, so you can judge every change.
pss_reload_desc: Reloads the shaders (compiling them only if the file changed) and rereads the luts folder without restarting the game.
pss_status_desc: Shows whether the plugin is hooked, compiled and processing frames.
pss_debug_view_desc: Shows one stage alone. Exposure paints red where it brightens; occlusion is grey; light effects show 4x brighter. Magenta checks: that effect is not running.
pss_inject_after_desc: 0 finds the game's finished image by itself. A number N runs the shaders after the Nth fullscreen pass instead. Only change this if a draw capture says so.
pss_require_fullscreen_desc: Only counts passes that cover the whole screen. Leave this on.
pss_menu_info_desc: What Screen Shaders does, what is new, and who made what.
pss_info_what_desc: A short overview of the shaders.
pss_info_what_text:
Screen Shaders runs its own shaders on the game world, after the world is drawn and before the HUD, so menus and the HUD are never touched.

It smooths edges, restores detail, adapts to light and dark, grades colour, and adds optional bloom, obscurance, colour bloom, monocular cues, lens dirt and halation. From the game's depth buffer it adds ambient occlusion, indirect light, ray traced lighting, reflections, haze and depth of field.

It only works on the picture the game has already drawn: it never sees anything the game does not already show you.
pss_info_others_text: Nothing. The shaders only change the picture on your own screen. Nothing is sent to other players or the host, and nobody needs the mod installed.
pss_info_new_desc: Release 0.7.5: a fourth preset, Enhanced (origin); Just the cleanup uses SMAA T2x.
pss_info_new_text:
0.8.0: this build joins two lines of the mod. AndreikaRPM's work on antialiasing - the tuned SMAA, SMAA T2x and the temporal antialiasing that reprojects last frame from the camera's own motion - comes in from their fork (codeberg.org/pd2-mods/ScreenShaders, 0.6.0 to 0.7.5), along with the fixes made there. On top of it: the moods (Lens: Hurt closes in, Stealth and loud), the step-aside in the weapon workshop, the Series hub entry, and the Enhanced look this mod has always shipped with as the default; AndreikaRPM's own look is a preset of its own.

The game's own antialiasing, ambient occlusion and depth of field are now handed back every time you quit, and only taken off while the plugin is really drawing. Removing the mod can no longer leave them switched off.

0.7.5: a fourth preset, Enhanced (origin): the original author's Enhanced look as 0.5.3 shipped it, without the Panini and spherical projections, which are gone, and with SMAA T2x instead of SMAA. Just the cleanup now uses SMAA T2x too.

0.7.4: depth of field's blur while aiming now works when no other effect needs the camera, as in the Clean look. Before, aiming was never seen there.

0.7.3: if the graphics card cannot make the buffers for lighting and motion, SMAA T2x now steps back to SMAA, as TAA already did. Before, the world went black.

0.7.2: SMAA T2x and TAA blend frames, which averaged the Dither noise away, so dark smooth areas could show colour steps again. The frame is now dithered once more at the very end, after that blend. Also: the plugin reads the camera file only right before each frame, no longer every 8 ms as well.

0.7.1: the long menu hints are cut to 200 characters at most, so the options stay readable.

0.7.0: SMAA T2x is the new antialiasing of the Enhanced look. The camera moves a quarter pixel one way and then the other, and each frame is blended half and half with the one before, so edges come out smoother than with SMAA, and something right in front of you leaves at most a faint echo for one frame instead of the trail TAA can leave. TAA still smooths more and is still there.

Antialiasing is one choice now: Off, FXAA, SMAA, SMAA T2x or TAA, instead of a switch, a method and a TAA switch that overruled each other. Your own choice carries over as whatever was running; press Enhanced at the top of the options to take SMAA T2x.

0.6.8: temporal antialiasing keeps its camera jitter. The check that the jitter really reaches the frames could be fooled while you stood still in front of many edges (railings, clutter, fences), and then paused the jitter for nothing, which made the picture less smooth for a while. It now compares only flat surfaces. In a full heist with it the jitter was never paused; every test heist since 0.6.1 had switched it off at least once. When the check does doubt a frame, mods/logs/pss_native.log says what the game was doing (downed, tased, the victory screen ...) and which cause fits.

0.6.3: when the camera jitter misses the frames for a moment (it happened for about a second mid-heist), it is paused and tried again after 10 seconds, then after longer waits if it keeps missing, instead of staying off for the rest of the level.

0.6.2: when the camera jitter does not reach the frames somewhere (it happened once near the end of a heist), it is now switched off for that level only, and checked again on the next. Before, the rest of the session went without it, which makes temporal antialiasing less smooth.

0.6.1: occlusion, bounce light, ray traced lighting and reflections now follow the camera from frame to frame, using the same cameras temporal antialiasing measures, instead of motion guessed from the picture. The guess followed the camera jitter badly, so with TAA on the lighting was blotchy even standing still; in a test room the error of ray traced lighting against a clean still view fell from 11.0 to 5.0 standing still and from 12.7 to 6.8 while moving, and of bounce light from 14.0 to 4.8 and 16.9 to 5.8. The picture search behind the guess now only runs for motion blur and surface grain, so motion and temporal in Plugin status should cost less.

0.6.0 is the release of the 0.5.21 to 0.5.36 work; nothing has changed since 0.5.36 but the version number.

Temporal antialiasing is rebuilt and on by default. Every frame is put back where your camera really is, from the depth and the camera itself, and the camera is turned by a fraction of a pixel each frame so edges are sampled in new places. The plugin checks from the depth that the turn really reaches the frames, and refuses it for the session if not; whenever TAA cannot run, SMAA does the antialiasing. In a test room against a 16-sample supersampled render, edge error is less than half of SMAA's standing still.

Two ideas from AMD's FSR 2 are in it: a surface that was hidden last frame, behind an enemy or a door that has moved, starts fresh instead of leaving a faint trail, and a just uncovered area averages its new frames at once instead of keeping its first, jagged one.

The Enhanced look is the author's own settings: TAA strength 1.0, bloom 0.3, the Film Stock LUT at 0.25 and vibrance 0.5, FSR off (1.5x when you switch it on). The FSR factor goes from 0.5x to 2x; below 1x it shrinks the finished frame and rebuilds it at screen size, which replaces Render scale cleanup. Your saved settings are kept, except that TAA is switched on once; press Enhanced at the top of the options to take the new look.

Fixed: while loading, the game can give a camera that is not a number, which turned frames black; it is now ignored.

0.5.20 makes sliders land on their own steps while dragged. Before, every value in between was applied, so dragging Upscale factor from 2x to 1.5x rebuilt the large FSR buffer about 25 times (1.63x, 1.61x, ...), which could hitch the game.

0.5.19 makes SMAA the default antialiasing and has it find edges by colour as well as brightness. Measured against an ideal edge, it removes about 82% of the stair-stepping where FXAA removed 60%: long, nearly level edges, low contrast edges and thin railings gain the most. Saved settings switch to SMAA once; FXAA is still one click away.

0.5.18 makes the depth effects cheaper without changing the picture. The game's depth is turned into distance once a frame instead of on every one of the hundreds of reads the effects make per pixel, and each surface position now reads its four depths in one fetch instead of four. Plugin status shows the new step as depth preparation.

0.5.17 fixes SMAA's edge blending. It blended in gamma space, which its authors' notes call the fallback: edges between a bright and a dark area came out too dark and thin. It now reads and writes the blend through sRGB views, as the reference intends. FXAA is unchanged.

0.5.16 removes the spherical (fisheye) projection. Like Panini before it, it warped the frame after the world was drawn but before the HUD, so waypoints and markers could never line up with what they point at.

0.5.15 makes Plugin status count frames where the shaders failed to run as frames without shaders (a failed compile used to show 0), and corrects the README and code comments that described the wrong defaults.

0.5.14 adds checks for the depth effects. Debug view (on the Tools page) can now show ambient occlusion, indirect light, ray traced lighting or reflections alone, and Plugin status shows how much GPU time each stage takes. Nothing about the picture changes.

0.5.13 keeps the compiled shaders in shaders/pss.hlsl.cache. Compiling held the game for a few seconds on every launch; now it happens once, after an install, an update or an edit to the shader, and later launches start the shaders straight away.

0.5.12 runs FSR's sharpener (RCAS) at screen size, where AMD runs it, instead of on the larger buffer where the resolve averaged most of it away. That drops one full-size pass and one large buffer. The same look now needs less: Upscale sharpness 0.45 matches the old 0.7, so it resets to 0.45 once, and higher values now go sharper than before. RCAS and the edge detection also match AMD's code exactly, and film grain is added last, after FSR and sharpening, so they no longer smear or harden it.

0.5.11 removes the Panini projection. It assumed a fixed field of view instead of your own, was not a true Panini mapping, and could never line up with the HUD, which is drawn after it. FSR upscaling is on by default again.

0.5.4 to 0.5.10 make the plugin work on Windows' own Direct3D 11: it hooks the game's real context, keeps up with d3d11 rewriting its draw entries, creates its pipeline state the way a single-threaded device requires, and the shaders now compile with Microsoft's compiler. The game's own antialiasing and ambient occlusion are only switched off once the shaders are really running. Bloom, vignette, depth of field, chromatic aberration and motion blur now ship off, and FXAA replaces SMAA.

0.5.3 leaves the game's own eye adaptation running, which brightens dark scenes a lot. The game adapts in HDR, before its tone mapping; this mod's adaptation works on the finished frame and can only trim, so switching the game's off was what made everything look too dark. The two do not fight, because this mod measures the frame before its own correction. It also removes the code behind the 0.5.2 crash altogether.

Security cameras are left as the game made them. The feed is an in-world monitor the game deliberately grades grey, and this mod's eye adaptation, depth of field, lens and grade were only darkening it, so the shaders step aside while you are on the cameras and come straight back when you leave.

It also finishes the 0.5.1 repair. That repair switched the game's light adaptation back on but left the game to write the change to disk later, and 0.5.1's crash on leaving a heist could throw it away - leaving the game dark, most visibly on camera feeds. It runs once more now, and every setting this mod changes is saved straight away.

0.5.2 fixes a crash on leaving a heist. Switching the game's own eye adaptation off was being re-applied on a timer, so it kept reaching into the world viewport while the level was being torn down - an access violation in the engine that no pcall could catch. It is now named once, re-applied only when the game itself puts its choice back, and never touched unless the viewport is alive.

0.5.1 fixes a dark game. Earlier builds turned PAYDAY 2's own light adaptation off, which this mod has nothing to replace, and remembered the old setting in memory only - so it stayed off after a restart and after the mod was removed. Light adaptation is left alone now, is switched back on once for anyone it caught, and the video options this mod does still turn off are written down so they come back.

0.5.0 reads the game's own depth, and ships as the author plays it.

PAYDAY 2's own antialiasing, ambient occlusion and depth of field are switched off while this mod is on, since it does all three itself.

Three presets at the top of these options switch the whole look in one click.
pss_info_credits_desc: Who made the techniques this mod builds on.
pss_info_credits_text:
AndreikaRPM - the antialiasing: SMAA tuning, SMAA T2x and the temporal antialiasing, with the camera measurement and frame sync they need, from the codeberg.org/pd2-mods/ScreenShaders fork (GPL-2.0-or-later), 0.6.0 to 0.7.5.

FXAA 3.11 after Timothy Lottes (NVIDIA).
SMAA by Jorge Jimenez, Jose I. Echevarria, Belen Masia, Fernando Navarro and Diego Gutierrez (MIT).
Contrast Adaptive Sharpening and FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 by AMD (MIT).
Dual filter blur after Marius Bjorge (ARM).
Depth of field after Dennis Gustafsson's single pass bokeh.
GTAO after Jimenez, Wu, Pesce and Jarabo (2016).
Motion estimation after the idea in AlucardDH's shaders (GPL-2).
Obscurance and edge separation follow Luft, Colditz and Deussen's unsharp masking of the depth buffer.
Native plugins loaded by SuperBLT.

Shaders, plugin, colour grades, lens dirt texture and menus by Copper.
pss_reset_page_desc: Puts every setting on this page back to its default.
pss_reset_all_desc: Puts every Screen Shaders setting back to the look it ships with.
pss_dialog_reset_page_text: Every setting on this page goes back to its default.
pss_dialog_reset_all_text: Every Screen Shaders setting goes back to the look it ships with.
pss_error_hint: Screen Shaders: $FEATURE switched off for this session after an error. Details are in the BLT log.
pss_menu_geometry_desc: Effects that use the game's own depth: ambient occlusion and depth of field.
pss_depth_mode_desc: How to read the game's depth buffer. Leave on Automatic unless the Depth view under Tools looks wrong.
pss_depth_near_desc: Only used when the depth buffer is projected. Ignored otherwise.
pss_depth_far_desc: The distance treated as fully far away. Haze and focus are measured against it.
pss_ao_on_desc: GTAO: real contact shadows in creases, corners and where objects meet. Flat surfaces are never darkened.
pss_ao_desc: How dark creases and contact areas get. Unlike Obscurance this knows what is actually touching.
pss_ao_radius_desc: How far around each point it looks, in world units. Larger is softer and broader.
pss_fog_on_desc: Distant surfaces lose contrast and take the colour of the air, the way real distance looks.
pss_fog_desc: How much distance drains contrast. It follows how bright the scene is, so night heists stay dark.
pss_fog_start_desc: How far away the haze starts, as a fraction of the far plane. Nothing nearer is touched.
pss_fog_tint_desc: Cool blue air at the low end, warm dust at the high end.
pss_dof_on_desc: Focuses on what you are looking at. Things nearer or farther soften like a real lens, with bokeh on bright lights.
pss_dof_desc: How much blurs away from the focus when you are not aiming. 0 keeps everything sharp from the hip.
pss_dof_focus_desc: 0 focuses on whatever is under your crosshair. Above 0 fixes the focus at that fraction of the far plane.
pss_dof_range_desc: How much either side of the focus stays sharp. Larger keeps more of the scene crisp.
pss_depth_view_desc: Shows what the mod reads as distance: near is bright, far is dark. A magenta checkerboard means no depth was found.
pss_dof_near_desc: How much things in front of the focus blur. At 0 only the background softens.
pss_dof_speed_desc: How quickly focus follows what you look at. Lower drifts like an eye; higher snaps.
pss_dof_weapon_desc: Your own weapon and hands are never blurred, and never pull the focus towards themselves.
pss_menu_lighting_desc: Light bouncing between surfaces, ray traced lighting and reflections, from the depth buffer.
pss_menu_atmosphere_desc: Distance haze, height fog, light glowing through them, and light shafts.
pss_il_on_desc: Light bounces off nearby surfaces onto others: a red wall tints the floor beside it.
pss_il_desc: How much bounced light lands on surfaces.
pss_il_radius_desc: How far away a surface can be and still light this one, in world units.
pss_rtgi_on_desc: Rays from each surface find what lights it. Screen space only: nothing off screen or hidden. Best with temporal on.
pss_rtgi_desc: How much of the light the rays find is added.
pss_rtgi_distance_desc: How far a ray travels, in world units. Longer finds more light and costs more.
pss_ssr_on_desc: Screen space reflections on floors, glass and water. Strongest at glancing angles, like real surfaces.
pss_ssr_blur_desc: 0 is a mirror; higher looks like polished concrete.
pss_temporal_desc: Averages occlusion, light and reflections over frames using motion vectors. Cleaner, but can trail in fast motion.
pss_hfog_on_desc: Fog that is thickest around your feet and thins upwards. Looking down into a room thickens it.
pss_hfog_desc: How thick the fog is at floor level.
pss_hfog_height_desc: How far up the fog reaches before it thins out, in world units.
pss_fog_glow_desc: The brightest light in view glows through distance haze and height fog.
pss_shafts_on_desc: Beams of light from bright windows and lamps, blocked by what is in front of them.
pss_shafts_length_desc: How far the beams reach from the light.
pss_ltm_on_desc: Balances dark and bright areas locally, so a dark corridor and a bright window both keep detail.
pss_ltm_desc: How strongly dark and bright areas are brought together.
pss_ltm_detail_desc: How much fine detail is lifted on top.
pss_mblur_on_desc: Blurs along the direction things move on screen, from motion vectors estimated from the picture.
pss_mblur_desc: How far along the motion the blur reaches.
pss_motion_view_desc: Draws which way each pixel moved instead of the picture. Grey means still.
pss_preset_enhanced_desc: The author's own settings: occlusion, bounce light, ray traced lighting, reflections, haze, shafts, gentle bloom, the colour grade and SMAA T2x antialiasing.
pss_preset_performance_desc: Keeps ambient occlusion, haze, tone mapping and the grade; drops the lighting effects that cost the most.
pss_preset_clean_desc: Antialiasing, light sharpening and debanding only. Vanilla PAYDAY 2 with the rough edges taken off.
pss_preset_andreika_desc: AndreikaRPM's own look, as their fork shipped it: no vignette or chromatic aberration, a gentler bloom, Film Stock at a quarter, no depth of field or motion blur.
pss_dialog_preset_text: This replaces all of your settings with that preset. Your keys are left alone.
pss_dof_aim_desc: The same, while your sights are up. It eases between the two as you raise and lower them.
pss_demoire_on_desc: Calms the shimmering pattern fine textures make at distance - fences, grates, tiles and brickwork.
pss_demoire_desc: How hard shimmering detail is eased towards its neighbours. Real edges are left alone.
pss_detail_on_desc: Amplifies the fine contrast a texture already has, so old surfaces read as having more detail.
pss_detail_desc: How much fine surface contrast is brought out. Held back at edges, so nothing rings.
pss_surface_grain_on_desc: Fine grain that travels with the surfaces instead of crawling over the screen, like a material's own texture.
pss_surface_grain_desc: How strong that grain is. Kept out of black areas and faded with distance.
pss_surface_grain_size_desc: How coarse the grain is. It shrinks with distance, the way a real surface's texture does.
pss_taa_desc: TAA only. How much of the accumulated picture is kept each frame. Higher is smoother and steadier; lower trails moving things less. Pixels that move take more of the new frame on their own.
pss_render_scale_desc: Below 1, the finished frame is shrunk and rebuilt at screen size. Loses detail, and takes the engine's aliasing with it.
pss_vanilla_restore_desc: Hands back the video options this mod switched off, and switches light adaptation on. Use it before removing the mod, or if an older build left your game dark.
pss_aside_workshop_desc: Turns the shaders off while you modify a weapon: the game draws it in a room of its own there, and the chain has nothing to add to a menu.
pss_vanilla_restore_none: Nothing needed putting back. PAYDAY 2's own video options are as you left them.
pss_vanilla_off_desc: Switches off PAYDAY 2's own antialiasing, ambient occlusion and depth of field, which this mod does itself. Turn it off to get your own settings back - do that before you remove the mod.
pss_taa_jitter_desc: For TAA and SMAA T2x. Shifts the camera a fraction of a pixel each frame for smoother edges; aiming is not affected. Starts a few seconds after loading in.
